title: Seat a robot gearbox's cartridge stack on its motor: find the hidden spline by feel, then square the housing
instruction: Fit the gearbox stack onto the motor and its input stage, fully seated with no gap, then let go.
context: Robot actuators are built by fitting planetary gearbox stacks to motors. The stack's input spline is hidden under it and turns freely of its housing, so it is found by twisting under light pressure, then the housing is turned back until its tabs drop in. REV's MAXPlanetary tips: "twisting the gear cartridges by hand slightly to line up the splines", "rotating back once the spline is engaged"; it must be "fully seated and no gap is present" before the screws go in.
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the bench (x forward, y to the robot's left); heights above the bench. Motor: REV NEO Brushless V1.1 (60 mm across, 58.25 long, 0.43 kg), unpowered, standing shaft up in a printed PLA stand screwed to the bench (80 x 80 x 30, 61 mm square pocket 25 deep, two M4 clamp screws; fixture/motor-stand-1to1.svg), axis at x 290, y 0; its face 63.3 up. Its 8 mm keyed steel shaft rises 35 from the face and turns freely. Input stage: REV MAXPlanetary Universal Input Stage (REV-21-2106), black aluminium, 50.8 square, 19.1 tall, screwed to the motor face square to the bench, its two ears (5.0 mm screw holes) at its far-left and near-right corners; its top face (the seat) is 82.4 up, with a 20.6 wide, 1.4 deep alignment notch in the middle of its left and right edges. Input coupler: REV 8 mm keyed input coupler (REV-21-2108), steel, 25.4 across, 39-tooth internal spline, on the shaft inside the input stage's bore, its top 1.2 below the seat. Stack, pressed together beforehand as the maker's steps say: 4:1 cartridge (REV-21-2102) at the bottom, 3:1 cartridge (REV-21-2101), 1/2 in hex output stage (REV-21-2104) on top; 50.8 square, 44.5 tall, 61.9 across its two ears, 0.40 kg. Under it: the 4:1 cartridge's input spline (39 teeth, 20.5 across, 4.2 long, on the sun gear, which turns inside the housing) and two alignment tabs (20 x 2 x 1.1) in the middle of two opposite edges. Cradle: printed PLA, loose, a 70 x 70 x 5 base with four 12 x 12 x 20 posts (fixture/cradle-1to1.svg); the stack stands on the posts, bottom face 25 up. Lot A (screenshot): cradle centre at x 200, y -140, cradle and stack turned 30 degrees counter-clockwise from square. Lot B: cradle at x 205, y +140, turned 30 degrees clockwise. Its input spline starts tooth on tooth with the coupler's at both square turns (0 and 180 degrees): in the simulation a quarter tooth (2.3 degrees) off meshing when square, one way in lot A and the other in lot B; in a real trial as the reset steps check. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Read with a feeler gauge, a ruler, a #10-32 screw and the trial video. 0 for the whole trial if at any moment the stack is let go of and falls (faster than 0.5 m/s, a fall of about 13 mm) or tips over (past 45 degrees). Every credited state needs both hands more than 5 mm from the stack and the stack still (nothing moving more than 1 mm) for 1 s. 1.0: seated: a 0.30 mm feeler leaf will not enter between the stack and the input stage at any of the four corners, and both of the stack's ear holes are within 0.5 mm of the input stage's (a 1-1/2 in #10-32 screw goes up through both and starts by hand). 0.5: spline engaged: on the shaft (axis within 1.0 mm), upright within 3 degrees, the four corner gaps averaging at most 2.0 mm, for example with its tabs standing on the face (1.1 mm) or turned 90 degrees. 0.25: threaded on the motor shaft (axis within 1.5 mm, upright within 5 degrees, bottom face less than 19.0 mm up) but higher, for example on the spline's tooth flats (3.0 mm). 0 otherwise, including left in the cradle or set down beside the motor. Trials are run on each of lots A and B and averaged.
run_limit: 800 steps (40 s at 20 Hz) per trial; two trials (lots A and B)
reset_notes: 1. Lift the stack straight off the shaft; if a stage has parted, press the three back together, ears in line. 2. Set the start phase: lower the stack onto the motor square, without twisting; it must stop on the tooth flats (a 2.5 mm leaf fits under every corner). Lift it, turn it half a turn and check again. If it drops in either way, lift it, turn its input spline a little with a fingertip from below, and repeat until both stop. 3. Lift it straight off without turning the spline and stand it on the cradle's posts, output stage up. 4. Set the cradle at the lot's place and turn, using the 1:1 drawing and a protractor.
fidelity: True size from REV's drawings. Rigid boxes and cylinders: 39 spline teeth with 0.10-0.15 mm side play and 0.10 mm tip chamfers (tooth count and chamfer estimated from the drawings), tabs with 0.3 mm play. The three stages are one body; only the input sun turns in it, against an estimated gear-train drag of 0.6 N m s/rad (motor shaft the same). Output stage mass and both drags are estimates. No screws: the job ends where they go in. Two lots stop a fixed habit, not a replay.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (mean of lots A and B, 800-step limit each; both arms rose and stayed over the table, never touching the stack); demo: 1.0 in each of lots A and B (seated, let go and still; each trial done at 608 steps)
